traces.question: Panel F1a overlays a fitted model on the measured diffraction data for the as-prepared porous cobalt oxide powder, together with a residual trace between the fit and the data. What does the fit indicate about the phase composition of the material, and how good is the agreement between the calculated curve and the measurement?

traces.question: Panel F6d plots the degree of oxidation over a 2-picosecond ab initio MD run, with curves labelled Li-Co3O, Na-C03S4, and Na-CoO and a y-axis marked in 20% increments up to 100%. Reading the curves in that panel, what is the difference in the degree of oxidation reached across these three conditions, and how does the sodiated cobalt-oxide curve behave over the course of the simulation?
traces.answer_key: At 2 ps, the degree of oxidation ranks Li-Co3O4 (~91%) above Na-Co3S4 (~59%) above Na-Co3O4 (~36%); the Na-Co3O4 curve plateaus after about 0.8 ps.

linear.text: Claim under test: Sodiation reduces PCO only slightly: crystalline oxide largely retained, no metallic Co
Read the panel: F2c [ECHEM]
Ruling: Na 1st discharge passes ~865 mAh/g, near the Li value, although structural probes show only minor reaction

traces.question: Given the claim above and the discharge/charge panel (F2c) offered as its evidence, what capacity does the panel actually show on the first sodiation, and does that reading fully back the claim as stated?
traces.answer_key: No, not cleanly. The panel shows the Na first discharge passing ~865 mAh/g, close to the Li reference value, even though structural probes indicate only a minor reaction (a2). The electrochemical capacity looks substantial, so the panel only partly backs the claim of a slight, largely-retained-oxide response — it qualifies rather than confirms it.
traces.grading: Answer key: the audit ruling on the panel, node a2.
